title: GPX Elevation Remover: Strip the <ele> Tags
description: Remove elevation elements from a GPX file with the GPX Elevation Remover — geometry untouched, altitude gone, locally in your browser. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, stripping <ele> from a typical trackpoint shrinks it from 97 to 81 bytes of XML — about a sixth of every point — while the latitude and longitude sit exactly where they were.
quick_answer: The GPX Elevation Remover strips the <ele> elevation elements from a GPX file and gives you a cleaned copy whose route geometry is untouched. Load the file, remove the altitude channel, and download the lighter copy — for privacy, compatibility, or wrong elevation.

body.t: Some sharing contexts want the line, not the vertical story. The geometry remains complete; the profile is simply not published. Its sibling strips the clock instead: the
A file whose altitude channel is corrupt (sea-level mountains, underground valleys) visualises badly everywhere. Removing the channel beats displaying confident nonsense.
Some minimal GPX consumers choke on elements they do not expect. A stripped copy is the lowest-common-denominator edition of the same track.
Elevation is a sixth of a typical point's bytes. For massive archives shared as geometry, the saving is real — and the original keeps the full record.

examples.label: Example · One point, before and after

body.t: Before: <trkpt lat="40.768100" lon="-73.971900"><ele>102.4</ele><time>…</time></trkpt> — 97 bytes. After: the same point without <ele> — 81 bytes. Coordinates and time untouched; only the altitude statement is withdrawn.

Elevation gain, loss and profile charts have nothing to read in the stripped file — they report absence, not zero. Keep the original wherever the vertical story matters; the stripped edition is for audiences who should not have it.

faq: Does the route still display on maps?
Yes — maps draw from latitude/longitude. The track shows identically in plan view; only profile and ascent features go quiet.

Not from the stripped file — but a map model can re-derive approximate elevation for the coordinates (DEM sampling). That is a model's estimate, not your recording's measurement, and honest tools label it so.
Altitude profiles can identify home floors, exact buildings and routines more precisely than a street path does. Stripping is a legitimate pre-share decision.
Real places sit below sea level and files carry 0 for missing data in sloppy exports — the remover removes the element whatever it says; it does not judge values.
Does it remove depth or altitude in extensions?
The standard <ele> channel is the scope. Exotic extension altitude fields are outside the GPX core this tool edits.
Both are stripped — <ele> appears in rtept and wpt too, and the remover walks the whole document.
